newsitem.title: PERU: Canada's guarantor says Peru attack "justifiable".
newsitem.headline: Canada's guarantor says Peru attack "justifiable".

text.p: Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent, a key player in negotiations for a peaceful solution to Peru's hostage crisis, said the violent raid that ended an 18-week standoff with Marxist rebels was "justifiable".
"Under the circumstances, with the results that had begun to happen, I think it was justifiable," Vincent said in Spanish during an interview with the local America television network.

Vincent, a hostage freed early in the siege to form a three-man talks' gurantors panel, said he never thought there should be a military assault on the Japanese ambassador's home where rebels held 72 hostages.
"But I have accepted that from the (Peruvian) government's point of view, this was always an option," Vincent said.
President Alberto Fujimori ordered elite troops to storm the diplomatic mansion on Tuesday after the jungle-trained guerrillas reduced the visits of Red Cross officials attending their captives.

Commandos executed two captured Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels and shot to death at least one other who was trying to surrender as they killed all 14 hostage-takers in the raid, security force sources said.
